rationale: Mara Voss built silhouette-first: five big masses (head, pauldron slab, coat, med-gun, boots) and nothing else. Head is rows 2-16 (15px) against a 61px figure — ~3.8 heads, cartoon-heavy. The one deliberate composition move is the oversized med-gun held level at the hip: a 12px-wide horizontal bar jutting fully clear of the left edge, the only horizontal in an otherwise all-vertical figure, so the outline has a landmark you can name from across the room. Balanced by an equally oversized bare fist low-right and a splayed 5px-crotch boot stance. Internal detail is rationed to five things that each do a job: visor, bone cross on the rust chest plate, belt, rust armband on one pauldron only (asymmetry), respirator grille. No dither, no stitching, no wear chips. Every material gets exactly two values plus the shared plum-black ink #120b10, which wraps the entire silhouette as one continuous contour (generated by an outline pass, not hand-drawn per part — that is what stopped the earlier drafts from fragmenting into floating rectangles). Light is upper-left, and top planes are explicitly lit — helmet crown, pauldron tops, boot toe caps — to sell the 2:1 dimetric down-angle. Palette is 24 colours: cold grey-plum coat, rust livery (#b1583a) and bone (#d6cfc3) as the medic ID, one desaturated teal for the visor. No magenta, no chartreuse. Sacrifices: zero facial nuance (she is a helmet and a mouth grille), the coat is a flat field between belt and hem, and the gun's internals are three pixels of suggestion — all traded for mass and outline. This will also be a pain to animate limb-by-limb since the arms are welded into the shoulder slab; it wants whole-body squash/bob, not an IK rig.
frontFacingCue: A 22px-wide visor band split by a 2px plum-black nose bridge into two lenses, each carrying an identical 3px specular at the same relative position — paired, symmetric highlights read as eyes and only work head-on. It is the brightest value on the sprite (#a8dcd4 / #f0fdf4) sitting directly against a hard ink frame above and below, so the contrast survives any downscale. Below it, three cues stack and all of them are bilaterally symmetric about column 23.5: an exposed skin band across the cheeks, a centred dark respirator grille with a lit metal lip, and cheek guards in helmet-shadow value dropping back on both sides. The head is also pushed clear of the shoulder line — jaw ends row 16, four rows of 6px neck with open transparent air on both sides, shoulders do not start until row 21 — so the down-angle cannot swallow it, and nothing (pack, weapon, canister) rises above the shoulder line to compete.
smallCheck: Honest verdict: it survives, with one casualty. Box-filtered to 21x28 the load-bearing reads all hold — the head stays a distinct block clear of the shoulders (the 4-row neck is what saves it; a 2-row neck did not), the visor collapses to a single bright horizontal dash that still reads as a face, the bone cross survives as a legible pale plus, the crotch gap keeps the legs separate, and the gun remains a recognisable mass sticking out to the left. What is lost: all weapon internals blur into one grey-and-rust smudge, so it reads as "she is holding something big" rather than "med-gun"; the pauldron armband, the belt buckle, and the knuckle catch-lights vanish entirely; and the respirator merges with the jaw shadow into a single dark mouth blob. Nothing turns into visual noise, which is the real test — it degrades to a simpler correct shape rather than to mush. If ~28px is the shipping size I would consider bumping the visor to 4 rows and dropping the armband, since it costs a colour and contributes nothing below ~40px.
